correctness.verdict: PASS - bit-for-bit agreement with scalar reference (any nonzero error would have been a real bug, not rounding noise)

device.clock: pinned to 2400000 kHz via performance governor (sudo tee scaling_governor); ondemand before/after
device.name: Mimir

method.inputs: deterministic dyadic rationals k/64, k in [-4,4]; every product and 64-term partial sum exactly representable in fp16, so kernel and reference must agree bit-for-bit
method.kernel: 8-wide SIMD inner k-loop (8x fp16 = one 128-bit NEON register); B pre-transposed so the k-loop streams two contiguous vectors; av.fma(bv, acc) -> NEON FMLA
method.timing: clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) via std.ffi external_call (pure Mojo, no libraries); 3 warmup matmuls, then 11 timed runs of 50 matmuls each; per-run ns/matmul reported

notes: 16.0 GFLOPS is ~21% of the Cortex-A76 NEON FP16 FMA roofline (~76.8 GFLOPS/core @2.4GHz); expected for a naive non-blocked kernel with no prefetching - this is a baseline, not a tuned result.

Mojo 1.1.0 API findings recorded in spikes/phase_a/neon_fp16_matmul.mojo header: no module-level alias, Pointer needs MutUntrackedOrigin from std.origin for mutable fn params, unsafe_load[W]() dtype-inferred, external_call clock_gettime for timing.
title: NEON FP16 64x64x64 matmul baseline (pure Mojo, native on Mimir)
